summary: Provides a small floating panel that opens beside a button, for example for a date picker or quick options.
purpose: Lets screens show extra content in a box that floats above the page.
why: Likely reason: it wraps a ready-made popover library and adds the app's styling and animation.
how: The trigger is the button that opens the panel. The panel is placed in a portal so it floats above other content. It is aligned and offset from the trigger by default, then styled with a border, shadow and animation. An anchor lets the panel be placed against another element.
inputs: Alignment and offset settings (center and 4 by default), plus children and style overrides.
outputs: A floating panel that shows and hides as the user clicks.
risks: The panel uses a fixed width, so long content needs an override. Its layering depends on a z-index class, so other fixed elements may cover it.
debug: If the panel does not appear, check the trigger sits inside the root and the open state is set. If it is hidden behind other items, check the z-index class.
